Tiny Homes

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:


The Tiny Home movement is about lowering your Carbon footprint, it’s about downscaling, living a minimalist life and basically decluttering to the essentials. Because we are all drowning in stuff that neither the planet nor us need.

The Tiny Homes movement has taken off around the world and is now slowly making waves in SA. On average they are between 8 – 20m2 in size and designed for maximum living in a minimum space. They come at a starting price of around R350k



Further information:
Matt is a live events organizer, who in 2019 decided to get a group of his friends together and bring the Tiny Home movement to South Africa

Matt and his wife and their bulldog have been living in their Tiny Home for over a year, it is 20m2. He says they created Wanderlust to show people that there is a different way to live, that we can save the planet, be mobile and free all at the same time.

A few years ago Aewon Wolf was on tour performing packed out gigs around the country, he was chasing the cash, surrounded by booze and girls, when he got a call that his father had had a stroke. He hadn’t been home in months and decided to take a two-week break. Two weeks turned into two years, as the high life began to lose its meaning to him. He started a journey to find himself again. It has been a roller-coaster, but today Aewon says he is closer to living his true life than ever before. He has a booming business that speaks to his soul, and he is selling the big house he bought in Westville to downscale into a Tiny Home at the coast. He has started the design with Matt and his team, and they are due to start construction in September. His main motivation is to rid his life of everything he doesn’t need to be truly happy

Marisa Visicale and Carla Cronjé’ sold up and build their own Tiny Home on wheels for R160k they are now living in a small town in the free state. They are both professionals that realised they can live anywhere and still do what they do. Their home has a view that goes on forever and the whole front opens up, so that the inside and outside become one.


Clara is an architect who build a tiny home for the food and wine expo in 2014 it was then shipped to Nirox and became their artist in residency accommodation. Carla is quite an academic architect and is very philosophical about the tiny home movement and its place in South African society

Flight to KZN x 1 and a car hire
Would you guys be willing to hire us a car to travel to the freestate in?
It is a 7 hour round trip

Script:


Tiny houses are all about downsizing and living with the bare minimum in a house often no bigger than 20 square metres . It’s a social and architectural movement centred around sustainable living solutions

MATT: The tiny house movement is IT’S for the environmentally conscious consumer who wants to downscale their carbon footprint and do something for the environment.

LINK: The tiny house movement has been popular in America and Europe for years, and now it's taking off in South Africa.

When COVID-19 hit it all but shut down Matt Bowers events focussed business, he needed a new plan. So, One morning after binge watching a tiny home series he woke-up and told his wife Kendal that he wanted to start building tiny houses in South Africa

Matt: She bought into the idea. And then when I said we need to move into the tiny house to prove that it's a liveable thing
And that's when she stormed out of the house. If bombs were dropping in tears

KENDAL: I COULDN’T INVISION WHAT IT WOULD BE LIKE. BUT THE MORE WE RESEARCHED INTO IT THE MORE I REALISED WHAT YOU CAN DO.

18 months ago Matt, his wife and their bull dog all moved into this tiny home. And used it as a prototype for their company wanderlust, which they formed with a group of friends.

Kendal: tour of the house

MATT: It's all about design and functionality of everything that you include in the home. Everything, almost everything has to have a double used to it.

CLARA:
in order to create a dual use for the shower, it is a place of passage because you only occupy it for two to three minutes when you showering.
Masa: So this is a passage and your shower.
That's right

Carla da cruz almeida is an architect that designed her first 14m2 tiny home in 2014 as a solution to student housing in South Africa. She exhibited it at a design fair and it was then moved to the Nirox sculpture park where it is now the artist in residency accommodation

Masa: what is the Tiny house movement all about
Clara: for me it was about trying to live bigger, but not using as much space.
So you live smaller in terms of the space that you want to be private in, but you live in your community

Clara verité: M: why there's a toilet in here as well.
C: It’s bigger, actually, than an airplane toilet.
C: So that is the only part that absolutely needs to be private,
and you close it
M: Now, you don't see me

MATT: The transition was quite simple. I've learned that it is possible to live with my wife in 20 square metres
But I've learned that we're all caught up with having too many belongings And every time you get a bigger house, you see there's an open space and just fill it. So you buy the decor items and you buy everything to fill it. And then when your house is full, you say, oh, my house is not big enough and it just becomes a snowball effect.

As part of the goal to lower their carbon footprint tiny houses are build using environmentally friendly, sustainable materials. Traditionally they are constructed in a factory, then placed on site.

Clara interview
construction actually accounts for something like 60 percent of carbon emissions.
when you have debris, when you demolish a building, that is what is not environmentally friendly. So the first thing we have tried to avoid is cement anywhere, even the foundations do not involve cement. Steel is better than concrete because steel can be reused. And wood is even better because even at the end of what you can put it in the braai and make a fire.

Tiny houses are normally built to be completely off the grid. They are fitted with a solar power system, grey water tanks and then various alternatives to sewerage disposal.

KENAL: 00:05:56:29 - 00:06:27:11
we are on a septic tank system on this land, but our toilet itself is a composting toilet, solid waste. We collect it into a bag and you toss that bag once a month. But the urine part of the composting toilet then goes into the septic tank system.


Vo: Two years ago Aewon was living a fast paced rock and roll lifestyle, he was on the road performing for months at a time. Until a family tragedy forced him to stop, stay at home and take stock

A1:
The more I focus on what really makes me happy, the more I started scaling down because I realized a lot of things are just distractions

Vo: He is now selling is big house and has contracted matt and his team to design him a tiny

Verite meeting - Matt about the size of the house

Aweone: You have this preconceived idea. Of success
And a big house has always been part of that. Success. A pitch that we've been sold
One thing I've learned is that it definitely isn't. Minimalist is the future,
It's actually a solution to this problem of consumerism

Aewone: So we actually going to clear this entire space here is that the sugar cane is going to be we're going to clear it so we can level and then the pod is going to be here

Aewones tiny house will be placed in the middle of his 2 hectare’s land, which he will turn into a homestead.

Aewone: when we build these big traditional houses, we kind of like forcing ourselves unnecessarily on the planet. And that's doesn't make sense to me anymore in terms of my lifestyle. I've got a motto that I live by now, which is Leave the World Better than you found it.

When South Africa went into a hard lockdown Debbie Agenbag and her partner moved from Pretoria to the farming town of Rosendal in the Eastern Free state where they build themselves a tiny home

Debbie: it has been in the back of my mind for quite some time that I would really love to scale down, simplify life, declutter, my life.
but I just never felt the opportunity was there. And then it presented itself

link: Three and a half hours from Johannesburg, Rosendal has become a hotspot for professionals looking to escape the city life and opting for a country life. And many of them are wanting tiny homes.

Debbie: it's literally like we live in a bubble. Sometimes you feel like the outside world cease to exist

Debbie is now the project managing on a lot of the tiny home developments in Rosendal, she took me around town to see a few of them

Masa: while Debs this is beautiful, it has exceeded my expectations
Masa: And how big is this place?
Debbie: This is 67 squeeze, really. So it is a proper tiny house

Vo: The Tiny homes that Debbie is working on are mainly fixed abodes. While Matt and Kendal are focused on the more traditional Tiny houses that are on a trailer and can be easily moved.

MATT: ultimate ideas to create what we term it as one as interconnected parcels of land across the country, whereby you can live in one plot or one of our states for six to 12 months, and then you can decide to move on to another one and create that freedom of movement for tiny homeowners.


Masa: who do tiny homes appeal to typically
Debbie: And I always thought it would be older people only it is done, And it's actually totally the opposite. It is people who want to give their kids space. They don't want the big houses either anymore. they want to focus their money in the effort and the time on on their kids

CLARA:
M: Why do you think the tiny home movement is gaining momentum in South Africa, particularly right now?
C: I think the economic pressure that the pandemic has put on many people, they've had to give up the costs that go into house ownership and I'd rather share for economic sustenance.

The actual per m2 building cost of a tiny house is not that much cheaper than a normal brick and mortar fixed home, but due to their sizes they are generally more affordable. On average they start at around 350 000 and can go up to 1.3 million depending on the size and finishes

MATT:
As a young South African you don't want to be going and signing up for a bond or mortgage that takes 20 to 30 years to pay off.
And you're not paying exorbitant amounts of interest to the bank over that period,
So You are able to reach financial freedom a lot sooner.
And also that extra money that you're able to save be allowed to spend on experiences so you can go traveling
it's certainly given me a new outlook on life and the way that needs to be lived.

link: This movement is the opposite of everything capitalism is ever taught us. It's all about living more by owning less.

DEBBIE: At the end of the day, it's not how many things you can tell other people you own and you have. It's about having a quality life and having a sustainable life and having a happy life.
Happy with her dog

Matt: the type of home that you have doesn't mean that you're not successful, doesn't mean that you're not wealthy. It's just a choice of life or choice of way of living.
sunset on the beach shots

CLARA:
For me, the core advantage of being in a micro house is that you become a better connected to your community,
and you have a tendency to expand it, to become more adventurous
If you live in a micro home, The entire world is your home.
